# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 3
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👏 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👏 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👏 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👊 👏 🤌 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👏 🤌 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👏 🤌 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👏 🤌 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 ✋ ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✊ 🙏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

**Board change — this is the headline.** The light was yellow for two rounds and is now BLUE. Display still 0, wires untouched. Mute has been working from "light = yellow" the whole time, so this new fact may be exactly what the manual's conditions are waiting on. I must relay it before anything gets cut.

**Decoding Mute's ten signs.** The structure is clean now that the clap 👏 acts as a separator: [👍] confirms my last reading; [2-no][3-no][1-yes] answers my cut question — target is wire 1; the pinch pairs repeat as 03, 11, 22, 31 even after I said no such numbers exist on the casing — so they're manual *conditions*, not markings, plausibly "display value → wire"; and the closing [🫳 ✋ ✊] [👎 ✊ 🙏] reads "hold — no — please": do not cut yet. That last part is why nobody's hands move this round, no matter how tempting "cut wire 1" looks.

**The convergence I can't ignore:** the light just turned the same colour as wire 1, and Mute's elimination says wire 1. But Mute signed "not yet" under the belief the light was still yellow. So I relay the colour change and demand tight thumbs-only answers: cut now or wait for the display? And one worked example to pin down the pinch-pair notation.

**Blind's two thumbs up** fit yes/yes to my two questions (feels the light, can order the wires). The orientation definition I proposed hasn't been confirmed yet, so I re-ask for a single thumbs up on "wire 1 = nearest the light," and ask Blind to report anything tactile about the light changing — Blind's hands are my only other sensor.

```
speak(text="Critical update for both of you: this round the indicator light CHANGED COLOUR. It was yellow, it is now blue. The display still reads 0. Wires untouched: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green. Nothing has been cut. Nobody cuts anything until Mute confirms the rule against this new fact.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your signs this round, as I read them: thumbs up, my reading was correct. Two-no, three-no, one-yes: the target is wire 1, the blue one. Palm-down, open-palm, fist, then no-fist-please: hold, do not cut yet. And your pinch pairs again: fist-pinch-three, one-pinch-one, two-pinch-two, three-pinch-one. Now the new fact: the light is BLUE, the same colour as wire 1. Answer each question in its own message, thumbs up or thumbs down only, finger counts for any number. One: does the blue light mean cut wire 1 now? Two: if not, must we wait until the display changes from 0? Three: do the pinch pairs mean first finger the display number, second finger the wire to cut at that number, so one-pinch-one means cut wire 1 when the display shows 1? Four: was fist-pinch-three an instruction for display 0 that is now void, or something else?")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, your two thumbs up I read as: yes, you can feel where the light sits, and yes, you can order the three wires in a row. Good. Do not cut anything yet. While we wait, confirm orientation with a single thumbs up: wire 1 is the wire closest to the light component, wire 2 the middle, wire 3 the farthest. If that does not match your hands, one thumbs down and nothing else. The light just changed from yellow to blue, so if the change is detectable by touch, tell me anything your hands notice on the case, one fact per message.")
```

TURN 4
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👏 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👏 ✌ 👏 🤟 👏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👊 👏 🤌 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👏 🤌 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👏 🤌 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👏 🤌 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 🫳 ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✊ 🙏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎]

**The light changed again: blue → dark.** So the light has now shown three states — yellow, blue, dark — while the display stays 0. Mute's model of the bomb is one step behind, so nothing gets cut this round; first I relay, then I test my new theory.

**What Mute's signs say now.** Four lone thumbs down, one per message — exactly matching my request to answer my four questions separately: no on "cut on blue," no on "wait for the display," no on my pinch-pair guess, and no on "03 is void." Then point-clap-yes, then **1, 2, 3**, then the pairs again: **03, 11, 22, 31**, then hold-please.

**New hypothesis, and it's coherent:** the pairs aren't wire assignments — they're the bomb's *states in order*, each pair = display number, then light code (1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 dark). Current reality: display 0, light dark = **03 — we are in the first listed state right now**, which is why "03 is void" got a no. The 1-2-3 is the cut order: wire 1 during 03, wire 2 during 11, wire 3 during 22, and 31 means it's over. This also explains "don't wait for the display" — the *light* is the clock, and the light already moved.

I can't verify any of this myself — Mute holds the manual. So I put the whole theory back as five thumbs-only questions, with the last one the go/no-go: is it safe for Blind to cut wire 1 while we're in state 03. If Mute confirms, my words reach Blind next round and the cut happens then.

**Blind's 👍👎** I read as: orientation confirmed (wire 1 = nearest the light), nothing else tactile to report — meaning Blind's hands can't sense the light colour, so I am the sole light sensor and must call out the state every round. I lock in the tactile layout and put Blind on standby for the exact phrase "cut wire N now."

```
speak(text="Update for both: the light changed again. It went yellow, then blue, and it is now DARK - off, no colour. Display still reads 0. All three wires intact. Also settled: Blind has confirmed the tactile order - wire 1 is nearest the light, wire 2 the middle, wire 3 the farthest. Mute, I have a new theory about your signs, and I need it confirmed before any wire is cut. Answer with one thumbs up or one thumbs down per message, in order.")
speak(to="mute", text="Question one: the four pinch pairs are STATES of this bomb, listed in the order they happen - first finger the display number, second finger the light code, where light one is yellow, light two is blue, light three is dark. So zero-three means display zero with a dark light. Thumbs up if yes. Question two: we are in state zero-three RIGHT NOW - display zero, light dark. Thumbs up if yes. Question three: your one-two-three with claps is the cutting order: cut wire one during state zero-three, wire two during one-one, wire three during two-two. Thumbs up if yes. Question four: at state three-one there is nothing left to cut, it is finished. Thumbs up if yes. Question five, the important one: it is safe for Blind to cut wire one NOW, while we are in state zero-three, and no other wire before that. Thumbs up if yes. If any answer needs more than yes or no, use finger counts in a separate message.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind: I read your thumbs-up thumbs-down as - yes, the order is confirmed, and no, your hands felt nothing else new. So to be clear: wire one is the one nearest the light component, wire two is the middle, wire three is farthest. The light has changed colour twice, so it is active, but you cannot feel its colour - only I can see it, and I will call the timing every round. Your instruction, when it comes, will be exactly this phrase: Blind, cut wire number N now. When you hear it, cut that one wire and nothing else. Until you hear that exact phrase, hands off. Sign one thumbs up when you are ready and know wire one by touch.")
```

TURN 5
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👏 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👏 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 🫳]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👏 🤌 ☝ ✊ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤌 ✌ ✊ 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤌 🤟 ✊ 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

**The decode of Mute's answers is complete, and the go-ahead is in.** The five lone thumbs map exactly to my five questions: four noes — my whole display/light "state" theory was wrong, and I drop it — and a **yes to question five: it is safe to cut wire 1 right now.** Mute then re-confirmed independently, in the established wire-verdict code: header [point-clap], then **1-yes, 2-no, 3-no**, then [point + palm-down] — the hold sign — which I read as: *cut wire 1 only, then pause before anything else.* Two independent confirmations of the same action from the one monkey who holds the manual.

**Why act this round and not ask again:** the light has cycled every single round — yellow, blue, dark. Mute's yes was given knowing the light is dark; if the manual keys on this dark-light window, waiting another round risks the window closing. Mute held twice before ("not yet" when the light was yellow, then blue) and has now released the hold. The manual holder's explicit yes plus an open window means the cut happens now.

**Blind's [👍]** answers my readiness demand: wire 1 is known by touch, waiting on my exact phrase. So Blind gets the promised phrase verbatim — cut only wire 1 (nearest the light), then hands off and report. To Mute I confirm what's happening and ask the only question that matters next: what signal ends the pause — light change, display change, or a fixed count — so I can time wire 2 correctly when the moment comes.

```
speak(text="Status for both: light still dark, display still 0, all wires intact. The decision is made. Mute answered my five questions with no, no, no, no, yes - my state theory was wrong on all four points and is dropped, but the yes on question five confirms it: safe to cut wire 1 now. Mute then re-confirmed the same thing unprompted - wire 1 yes, wire 2 no, wire 3 no, then a hold sign, which I read as: only wire 1, then pause. The cut is happening this round, inside the dark-light window.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, cut wire number one now. That is the wire nearest the light component, first in your confirmed order. Cut only that one wire. Then take your hands off the bomb entirely and touch nothing else. When it is done: one thumbs up if the bomb sits quiet under your hands, one thumbs down if you feel anything change. Do not start anything further - I will call the next step myself.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your go-ahead is received and acted on - Blind is cutting wire 1 this round, only wire 1, then pausing. Confirm my reading of your last block: the cut is wire 1 yes, wire 2 no, wire 3 no, and the point with palm-down means wait before the next cut. One thumbs up if correct. Then one question, answered with finger counts in a separate message: after wire 1 is cut, what ends the pause before wire 2? One finger if we wait for the light to change away from dark, two fingers if we wait for the display to leave 0, three fingers if we wait a fixed number of rounds - and if three, give the number in a following message. Your final three messages - one-pinch-one then fist then yes, then pinch-two-fist no, pinch-three-fist no - I have not decoded yet. If they matter for the timing of wire 2, re-send their meaning using finger counts and yes and no only.")
```
